💰 Budget & Costs

Tourism Costs in China

Detailed guide to prices and daily budget – hotels, transport, food, entrance tickets

💰 Price Guide⏱️ 7 min read
Home›Tourism in China›Tourism Costs

One of the most common questions travelers ask: Is China cheap or expensive? The answer is that China is an affordable destination compared to Europe and America, with options to suit all budgets. Arcadia Tourism offers tour packages at competitive prices starting from $1,200 per person for 10 days.

Expected Daily Budget 📊

Budget tier: approximately $50–80 per day (3-star hotel + public transport + local meals). Mid-range tier: $100–180 per day (4-star hotel + mixed transport + varied restaurants). Luxury tier: $200+ per day (5-star hotel + private car + upscale restaurants).

Hotel Prices in China 🏨

Hotel prices vary by city and season. In Beijing and Shanghai: 3-star hotels from $40–70, 4-star from $80–150, 5-star from $150–400 per night. Prices in smaller cities are 30–50% lower. We recommend booking early, especially during peak tourist seasons.

Transportation Costs 🚄

High-speed trains: Beijing–Shanghai is approximately $80–90 for second class (4.5 hours). Metro in major cities: $0.50–1 per trip. Taxis are very affordable starting from $1.50. Check our travel tips for the best ways to get around.

Food Prices 🍜

Meal at a local restaurant: $3–7. Meal at a mid-range restaurant: $10–20. Halal restaurant: $5–15. Coffee: $3–5. Bottled water: $0.30–0.50. Chinese cuisine is diverse, delicious, and very reasonably priced.

Entrance Ticket Costs 🎫

Great Wall of China: $6–9. Forbidden City: $8–12. Terracotta Army: $20. See our attractions guide for full details. Most public parks and smaller temples are free or have nominal fees.

Arcadia Packages 📋

We offer all-inclusive packages starting from $1,200 per person / 10 days including accommodation, guided tours, transfers, and an Arabic-speaking guide. For business trips, special packages are available tailored to your needs.

💡 Tips to Save on Costs

Avoid traveling during Golden Week (early October) and Chinese New Year (February). Use high-speed trains instead of domestic flights – cheaper and more enjoyable. Eat at local restaurants for the best value for money.
